item.title: Ohio man fleeing police on foot leaps onto moving car, tries to take control before falling off: Police
item.description: Dramatic video shows Ohio shoplifting suspect Kaamil O'Berry leaping onto a woman's car on I-75 and clinging to her windshield during a police chase.
item.content:encoded:
An Ohio man accused of shoplifting leaped onto a woman's car as she barreled down the highway trying to escape police, dramatic video shows.

Two Ohio men accused of shoplifting from a Kroger were pulled over by Miami Township police on July 27, and one of them, later identified as Kaamil O'Berry, bolted from the car and fled on foot, according to WKRC.

The suspect was seen running over the on-ramp to I-75 as he ran away from police.

As O'Berry allegedly continued to run from police, he was seen running onto the interstate and jumping onto the hood of a woman's car, who continued driving.

LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

The suspect clung to the hood of the woman's car until both vanished from the highway camera's view, allegedly attempting to take control of the car. He broke her windshield in the process as well.

Eventually, O'Berry fell off the woman's windshield and was arrested. He was transported to a nearby hospital, according to the report.

O'Berry was arrested on charges of obstructing official business, theft and aggravated robbery.

David Sutter, who was in the car with O'Berry, was charged with complicity to theft.

item.title: Lions lament Terrion Arnold absence as he could join troubling list of NFL players who derailed their careers
item.description: Terrion Arnold faces life in prison on armed robbery and kidnapping charges as the Detroit Lions lament losing their former first-round cornerback.
item.content:encoded:

The newest part of the Arnold story is how the Detroit Lions, who drafted the cornerback in 2024 and were expecting him to mature from their secondary's most promising player to its star, are still lamenting everything that has transpired.

"Listen, I'm not going to say it was a setback, so to say, because to me, honestly, that's disrespectful to the guys that's still in this locker room," Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard told reporters on Sunday.

"What I'll say is Terrion Arnold had number one cornerback potential, but it was still untapped. You know what I mean? And I'll kind of leave that at that."

He has been charged with four counts of armed robbery with a firearm or deadly weapon and four counts of kidnapping. Arnold's legal representation has denied the allegations but that didn't stop the Lions from releasing Arnold on the day of his first court appearance.

item.title: FIRST ON FOX: Trump to open direct line with military families in ground-up readiness push
item.description: Trump's executive order creates a Military Spouse Commission chaired by Jennifer Hegseth to address childcare, housing, employment and healthcare.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: President Donald Trump is expected to sign an executive order on Monday creating a new White House commission aimed at putting military families at the heart of military readiness, Fox News Digital has learned.

The executive order would establish the President's Military Spouse Commission, which would advise the president on policies affecting military spouses and families and provide annual recommendations to improve their quality of life while strengthening military readiness, a White House official told Fox News Digital.

The commission is designed to give the White House a direct line to the challenges facing military spouses, including childcare, employment, housing, healthcare, education and the demands of multiple deployments.

PENTAGON FIRES BACK AFTER MARK KELLY ACCUSES PETE HEGSETH OF TARGETING WOMEN AND BLACK MILITARY OFFICERS

Trump is expected to sign the order Monday afternoon alongside War Secretary Pete Hegseth, his wife Jennifer, Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff Gen. Dan Caine, and several military spouses, the official said.

The Military Spouse Commission will be chaired by Jennifer Hegseth.

Trump will appoint an executive director, while Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin's wife, Christie Mullin, and 20 other military spouses representing the service secretaries, Joint Chiefs of Staff and each branch's senior enlisted leader will serve as commission members.

TRUMP ADMIN'S PUSH TO SCRAP DEI IN FEDERAL GOVERNMENT TAKES LANDMARK STEP WITH NEW HIRING RULE

Military spouse employment and pay are the top concerns for active-duty military families, followed by time away from family, childcare, housing and housing allowances, and children's education, according to Blue Star Families' latest Military Family Lifestyle Survey.

An estimated 1 million children have at least one parent serving on active duty, according to government website Military One Source.

During his first term, Trump expanded support for military families by improving occupational license portability for military spouses, broadening access to remote and flexible work, and increasing opportunities for federal employment.

GOLD STAR WIDOW SAYS 'BLESSINGS ARE INFINITE' AFTER STRANGERS FLOOD HUSBAND'S ARLINGTON GRAVE

In 2018, Trump also signed legislation allowing military spouses to claim the same state of legal residence as their active-duty spouse, even when military orders require the family to move elsewhere.

In a Military Spouse Day proclamation signed in May, Trump said the nation's 250 years of freedom were made possible by the armed forces and the "selfless spouses" who have shared in the burden of military service across generations.

He acknowledged at the time "more work is needed" in relation to employment, quality housing, affordable childcare, accessible healthcare and education for military families.

"In times of peace and in the crucible of conflict, they rise to meet every challenge and bear the pressures and sacrifices with relentless grace and fortitude," the proclamation read.

item.title: New Jersey government under congressional investigation after explosive revelations on noncitizen voters
item.description: Jim Jordan and Bryan Steil demand documents from New Jersey on federal voting law compliance after 6,600 noncitizens were added to voter rolls.
item.content:encoded:
House Republicans are probing New Jersey's government after Gov. Mikie Sherrill admitted to more than 6,000 noncitizens being added to Garden State voter rolls in 2023 and 2024.

The GOP has been hammering New Jersey Democrats ever since Sherrill announced that 6,600 noncitizens were mistakenly added to the state's voter rolls during that two-year period, before she was in office, as election integrity sits as a key focal point ahead of the November midterms.

Judiciary Committee Chairman Jim Jordan, R-Ohio, and Committee on House Administration Chairman Bryan Steil, R-Wis., wrote to New Jersey Lt. Governor Dale Caldwell on Monday for more information on the state's compliance with federal laws surrounding elections.

HOUSE REPUBLICANS CONFRONT NJ GOVERNOR OVER 6,600 NONCITIZENS REGISTERED TO VOTE IN ALLEGED SOFTWARE FAILURE

"During a July 21, 2026, press conference, New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill announced that approximately 6,600 noncitizens were registered to vote between June 2023 and June 2024 because the state Motor Vehicle Commission (MVC) sent the information of noncitizens who accurately marked they were not citizens to the Department of State’s Division of Elections and the noncitizens were then registered to vote," Jordan and Steil wrote.

"According to Governor Sherrill, around 400 of these individuals successfully voted in elections since 2023. We write to express our serious concerns with New Jersey apparently adding thousands of noncitizens to its voter rolls and to request information from the New Jersey Department of State about its compliance with applicable federal voting laws."

Sherrill attributed the mistake to a "serious software error in New Jersey’s Motor Vehicle system."

GOP ERUPTS OVER 6,600 NONCITIZEN VOTERS FOUND IN BLUE STATE AS SCANDAL DEEPENS: ‘WORSE THAN ANYONE EXPECTED’

But it's unclear how many noncitizens have been able to register to vote beyond those two years, thanks to New Jersey motor voter laws that make it easy for people to go through that process during a visit to their local Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) location.

The revelations appear to undercut Democrats' assurances that noncitizens are not voting in U.S. elections, while feeding into Republicans' push for stricter federal standards at the ballot box. To date, however, there has been no evidence that shows noncitizens have swayed the outcome of any federal election.

"The vendor, IDEMIA, that provided the software that Governor Sherrill alleges caused the noncitizens to be registered refuted Governor Sherrill’s claims, stating that New Jersey agencies were to blame," the Republicans' letter said. "According to IDEMIA, the registration of noncitizens appears to have ended only when MVC asked IDEMIA to change certain settings in June 2024, but the noncitizens were not removed from the voter rolls and the issue was not publicly disclosed until now."

FEDERAL JUDGE BLOCKS DOJ ACCESS TO NJ VOTER ROLLS AMID STATEWIDE CONTROVERSY

"If the New Jersey government had access to accurate information about the citizenship status of the noncitizens who were registered to vote and were aware of the situation in June 2024, this raises additional questions about Governor Sherrill’s decision to blame IDEMIA, to not remove the noncitizens from the voter rolls, and to not disclose the issue to the public."

They pointed out that Caldwell, as the top elections official in the state, is "uniquely positioned" to help with House Republicans' investigation.

The committees are now seeking any and all information related to New Jersey's compliance with the Help America Vote Act of 2002 (HAVA), the National Voter Registration Act of 1993 (NVRA), and the Civil Rights Act of 1960 (CRA).

"HAVA governs the rules, maintenance, and technical coordination required for statewide voter registration databases. The NVRA mandates that state motor agencies serve as voter registration portals with requisite compliance protocols to maintain accurate and up-to-date voter rolls. The CRA requires states to maintain voter records and empowers the U.S. Department of Justice to vet voter rolls by cross-referencing lists to identify improper registrations," the letter said.

They're also looking for any documents pertaining to how New Jersey vets its voter rolls for eligibility as well as evidence of a "lack of cooperation" with the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) in its aim to verify the citizenship status of each state's voters.

The letter is also signed by Rep. Jeff Van Drew, R-N.J., and Rep. Laurel Lee, R-Fla., both of whom chair relevant subcommittees on the matter.

They are requesting that New Jersey's government provide the documents by no later than August 17.

Fox News Digital reached out to Sherrill's office for comment.

item.title: Montana teen throws lasso to man in Yellowstone River in split-second rescue
item.description: A 14-year-old Montana rancher lassoed a drowning man from the Yellowstone River after a rafting accident, using cowboy skills he recently learned.
item.content:encoded:
A 14-year-old Montana rancher-in-training says God put him in the right place at the right time after he used the cowboy skills he'd spent months practicing to lasso and rescue a drowning man from the Yellowstone River following a rafting accident.

Jory Thomas was camping with his family near Greycliff, Montana, on July 5 when they heard someone screaming for help.

"We all heard, 'Help, help,'" Thomas told KTVQ. "There's two or three people floating down the river, one hanging on to the cooler, and he wasn't saying anything."

CALIFORNIA LIFEGUARD SPEAKS OUT ON HEARTSTOPPING OCEAN RESCUE: 'I LOVE WHAT I DO'

A raft and paddleboard had struck a bridge pillar, throwing four people into the river. Three reached shore, but one man continued drifting downstream while clinging to a cooler.

Thomas said there was no time to wait.

"This current was pretty fast then, and he was moving pretty quickly," he said. "Only thing I could focus on was helping him get out of the water because I didn't want to see anyone go in front of me."

He emptied his pockets, crossed a waist-deep side channel and ran along the bank. Then he grabbed a 12-foot lariat he'd brought from home — something his grandmother told the station he'd never packed for a camping trip before.

"My first instinct, I thought, was try and rope him and drag him out before he gets too far down the river," Thomas said. "Luckily, I caught him first try."

Thomas pulled the man toward shore through chest-deep water until first responders arrived.

OFF-DUTY ICE OFFICER RELIES ON 'SIXTH SENSE' TO SAVE DROWNING CHILD BEFORE DELIVERING MESSAGE TO CRITICS

The teenager said he'd only started taking roping seriously this year while helping with cattle on the family ranch, telling the station that his skills improving the more he roped cattle.

Thomas said he believes his faith guided him to act.

"God was basically putting me in the place of all this," he said. "God was just telling me all of this at the time and saying, 'Go get him, you got it, and I believe in you.'"

He later reflected that he never expected the same skills he learned on the ranch would save a person's life.

"I just thought I could help with cattle," Thomas said. "Not really helping humans and stuff like that. But I'm glad I was here to help."

The Sweet Grass County Sheriff's Office later honored Thomas with a Certificate of Achievement. Sheriff Alan Ronneberg and Undersheriff Ron Swanson recognized the teen for rescuing the man near Pelican Fishing Access.

"Well done, Jory!" the sheriff's office wrote in a social media post.

item.title: Michael Thorbjornsen 'finally' arrives, Patrick Cantlay's gutless decision, and the FedEx Cup playoff bubble
item.description: Michael Thorbjornsen fired a bogey-free 63 to win the Rocket Classic, while Patrick Cantlay's puzzling strategy on a drivable par 4 raised eyebrows.
item.content:encoded:
Well, we're still waiting for that post-final major championship of the year hangover to set in.

A week after Jackson Koivun picked up his first win on the PGA Tour in just his third start as a professional, Michael Thorbjornsen earned his maiden victory on Tour at the Rocket Classic, making it back-to-back weeks that two of American golf's most highly anticipated players found the winner's circle.

While it has felt like a long time coming for Thorbjornsen to cross the finish line from an outsider's perspective, it's fair to say the wait has felt significantly longer for the 24-year-old himself after the journey he's already been on in his young career.

CHARLEY HULL PULLS OFF SAVAGE LOTTERY PRANK ON HER CADDIE AT WOMEN'S BRITISH OPEN

Speaking of a long time, it has been nearly four full years since Patrick Cantlay won a golf tournament, and based on his strategy during Sunday's final round at the Rocket, he seems perfectly content with that reality.

Finally, this weekend will mark the end of the PGA Tour regular season. As per usual, there are some big-time names on the outside looking in when it comes to punching tickets to the FedEx Cup Playoffs. We'll take a look at them and toss some predictions out there.

This is Par Talk, a weekly read to get you caught up on all the happenings that took place in professional golf that you need to know. You can follow Mark on X @itismarkharris and email him at mark.harris@outkick.com.

It's not entirely fair to pin the statement 'it's a matter of when, not if this player wins on the PGA Tour' on someone, because winning on the PGA Tour is outrageously difficult. Michael Thorbjornsen, however, has certainly had that sentiment attached to his name for years now.

It took Thorbjornsen 65 starts on Tour to earn his first victory, and while that number may seem somewhat large, context is supremely important to look at in the case of his career.

In August 2023, he suffered a stress fracture in his back that forced him to miss out on playing in the U.S. Amateur and a spot on the U.S. Walker Cup team. Later that same year, he underwent ankle surgery while still recovering from his back injury. He's also withdrawn from multiple PGA Tour events mid-round due to other injuries.

While overall he's hit the ground running since turning professional in June 2024 with 40 made cuts and 20 Top 25 finishes in his 64 previous starts before finding the winner's circle at the Rocket Classic, he's dealt with some battles most players in his age bracket avoid.

With all that in mind for the former Stanford standout, his come-from-behind win and slamming of the door on the 72nd hole made for a compelling scene on Sunday afternoon.

Thor began the day four shots off the lead, and while knowing he'd need his best stuff to climb to the top of the leaderboard, he went out and fired a bogey-free 63 to eventually snag a two-shot victory. It's worth mentioning he did so while playing alongside major champion Xander Schauffele, who was firmly in the mix on the back nine on Sunday as well.

Thorbjornsen has some catching up to do when it comes to fellow 24-year-old Tour players like four-time winner Tom Kim and three-time winner Akshay Bhatia, but it has been abundantly clear he has the tools, the speed, and a sneaky great game around the greens to jump into the upper echelons of players, not just younger players, on the PGA Tour.

Patrick Cantlay began Sunday's final round five shots back of the lead. Sure, that's a large deficit to try and erase, but firing a low round in the 60s and seeing what the leaders end up doing behind you seems like a game plan to implement when you're a guy searching for your first win since August 2022.

After getting to 2-under for the day through his opening five holes, Cantlay carded a bogey on the Par 4 7th hole, which is forgivable given it played as the hardest hole on the course on Sunday. He then sent a clear, embarrassing, and sad message on the eighth tee.

The Par 4 8th hole was the easiest hole on the golf course for the final round, playing at just 332 yards and drivable for a large chunk of the field. The overwhelming majority of players attempted to drive the green, and at worst, left themselves a chip shot of less than 20 or so yards, giving them a great opportunity at birdie, or maybe even an eagle.

Cantlay opted to hit an iron off the tee, leaving himself 130 yards to the pin. Mind you, Sunday's final round was played under lift-clean-and-place conditions given the rain the golf course had taken on overnight. The greens were incredibly receptive, and controlling spin with a full wedge shot as opposed to a chip shot makes the eighth hole significantly more difficult, but clearly, Cantlay didn't see it that way.

He ultimately hit his approach shot to 21 feet, missed the birdie putt, and walked away with a lifeless par.

Cantlay finished T-8, and of the 13 other players who finished T-8 or better, only Hideki Matsuyama and Michael Kim chose to lay up on the eighth as he did.

This week's Wyndham Championship is the final opportunity for players to earn a Top 70 spot in the FedEx Cup standings, earn a spot into the FedEx St. Jude Championship in Memphis, and keep their seasons alive, and there are some notable names who have to have big weeks in order to accomplish that.

Keegan Bradley (72), Jason Day (75), Brandt Snedeker (83), Brooks Koepka (86), Tony Finau (89), Lucas Glover (96), and Billy Horschel (107) will start the week on the outside looking in. That list of players has a combined eight major championships and two FedEx Cup titles between them. Despite winning just two weeks ago, Koivun is the bubble boy, beginning the week at No. 70 in the standings.

Of the names listed above, it's going to take each of the guys outside the Top 80 to have huge weeks to earn a spot in the field in Memphis. Snedeker's name stands out as a two-time Wyndham Championship winner. While Sneds has great history to lean on, Koepka has played the event just three times in his career, with the last being a missed cut in 2020.

Let's go out on a limb, however, and predict Koepka finally puts it all together this week, does enough and gets enough help as well, to sneak inside the Top 70.

item.title: 'The Exorcist' star Linda Blair speaks out after home searched in reported 100-dog kennel investigation
item.description: "The Exorcist" star Linda Blair says she and over 100 dogs are fine after Los Angeles County officials executed an inspection warrant on her rescue property in extreme heat.
item.content:encoded:
Linda Blair is speaking out after authorities searched her Southern California property as part of an active investigation into a reported kennel operation allegedly housing more than 100 dogs.

"The Exorcist" star, 67, said she and the animals in her care are "good" after a "surprise" visit from Los Angeles County officials on Friday.

Officials executed an inspection warrant as part of a joint operation between the Los Angeles County Department of Animal Care (DACC) and Control and the Los Angeles County Department of Regional Planning, according to People magazine. Officials told the outlet the operation was intended to evaluate the welfare of the animals and determine whether the property complies with county regulations.

"Checking in, I’m good. The animals are good in lieu of our surprise visit in 105° heat! With as busy as we all are in animal rescue and saving lives from the hot deserts and abandoned animals and shelters, everyone’s emails and social media are overloaded," Blair captioned a video posted to Instagram on July 31.

'EXORCIST' STAR LINDA BLAIR 'UNKNOWINGLY' WALKED AWAY FROM HOLLYWOOD

"Turns out we just have some paperwork to do and some diagrams but as everybody knows, I’m looking to move so I can be more educational and help more animals. I’d rather move forward," she continued. "And I always say you know a good old-fashioned letter of contact always works. Be safe safe lives support animal rescue cause we’re all fighting to save lives.

The Oscar-nominated actress added that she has been planning to relocate her rescue operation.

The search was conducted after authorities sought to inspect a property "associated with a kennel operation reported to have more than 100 dogs," per People.

Officials alleged the kennel permits expired in 2023 and claimed multiple attempts to contact the property owner had gone unanswered.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

"The warrant allows us to lawfully access the property and verify compliance with County codes," the department said in a statement to People, adding that investigators were assessing "animal care, safety conditions, and overall welfare of the dogs housed on the property."

"Our priority is the safety and well-being of both the animals on the property and the people who may be working or residing here," the statement continued. "This inspection will help us determine whether conditions meet required standards."

The DACC said the matter remains an active investigation and declined to provide additional details.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"As this is an active and ongoing investigation, DACC is not able to answer specific questions about this case at this time," the department said, adding that it is committed to ensuring kennel operations meet legal requirements and provide humane care.

TMZ, which first reported the search, said Blair was present during the inspection and cooperated with authorities. No dogs were removed from the property, according to the outlet.

In a video accompanying her Instagram post, Blair reiterated that the visit centered on administrative issues rather than the animals' condition.

"Today we got a really big surprise visit," she said in the video. "And as it turns out, there is nothing but some paperwork and some new diagrams and things."

"Wanted to check in and let you know I am fine. The animals are fine. And we just have some paperwork that has to be dealt with. And that's all this was all about. I don't know why mail isn't used more often to notify somebody. Just saying," she said, while also encouraging supporters to donate to the Linda Blair WorldHeart Foundation — the nonprofit she founded in 2003 to rescue and rehabilitate abused, neglected, and abandoned animals.

She ended her video by reiterating how she and the animals are doing, saying, "I wanna let you know I'm ok and so are the animals. Thank you so much."

Representatives for Blair and the Los Angeles County Department of Animal Care and Control did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

item.title: 49ers betting preview suggests Rams and Seahawks could overtake San Francisco for playoffs
item.description: The San Francisco 49ers boast elite talent on paper, but recurring injuries to Nick Bosa, Fred Warner, and George Kittle raise serious concerns.
item.content:encoded:
Technology is fun. I wrote this article once already, and something happened where it disappeared altogether. I really don’t know what the issue is or was, but maybe the second time I dissect the San Francisco 49ers' upcoming season will be even more exciting than the first time.

This was a team that I struggled to bet on or against last season. When I was betting they would lose, they came out with some miracle game. When I bet they would win, they looked like they had never played football before. I can still admit that the squad was impressive despite navigating a wide range of injuries. They were 12-5 for the season and got a 5-3 record from their backup quarterback, Mac Jones. Every loss they took in the regular season was against a postseason team, with the exception of Tampa Bay. They did win the first game of the postseason, taking out the reigning Super Bowl champion Eagles. Then disaster struck against the Seahawks. They gave up a game-opening kickoff return for a touchdown. Then turned the ball over on downs, leading to a Seattle field goal. A fumble and another Seattle touchdown put them down 17-0 after the first quarter. The second half was even worse in many ways. They turned the ball over on downs, then had an interception, turnover on downs, fumble, punt, and then ran three meaningless plays to end the game.

49ERS BRING BACK DEEBO SAMUEL TO FILL VOID LEFT BY RICKY PEARSALL'S KNEE INJURY: REPORT

The team that deals with many injuries at many positions took a shot with someone uber talented, but also coming off of an injury-marred season. Mike Evans, who played only eight games last season, is now their primary receiver. If he is healthy, which he has been most of his career, he will be a difference-maker. They also added Christian Kirk, providing quarterback Brock Purdy with some solid options. It seems like they assumed offense was the priority, considering they also drafted a wide receiver in the second round. Their main addition on defense was Osa Odighizuwa; if he can replicate his season from last year, this should be an even tougher defense.

49ERS HAVE SUCCEEDED WITH TALENT ACQUISITIONS BUT FAILED AT ADDITION BY SUBTRACTION OF BRANDON AIYUK

The biggest issue I have with the 49ers is that they don’t ever seem to be healthy. There is a ton of talent on this roster, but if you look at the names on paper and those who are actually available, there is a large gap. Christian McCaffrey is one of the best backs in the league, but he misses games fairly regularly. Brock Purdy consistently misses games. Nick Bosa and Fred Warner both played fewer than 10 games last season. George Kittle is on the PUP list to start the year. Ricky Pearsall has some issues with his knee again as well. Healthy, they are elite, but that’s going to be a major question mark for this team all season.

Their head coach, Kyle Shanahan, has been great at getting the most out of his team regardless of who is on the field. However, I have some concerns that as these players age, they may not be able to go as far as long. No team will be healthy the whole season, but some of these guys are more consistently off the field than they are on the field. At 9.5 games, I don’t love taking the over – even though I think it hits, but you’re playing it at -145 or higher. Instead, I think we bet that there are going to be pieces missing and the Rams and Seahawks will still be better. I’ll take San Francisco to miss the playoffs at +122 if I had to take anything. Most likely I’ll just stay away.

item.title: Trump's AG pick off life support after key Republican rebels relent
item.description: Todd Blanche's AG confirmation has new life after Sens. John Cornyn, R-Texas and Thom Tillis, R-N.C., said they were satisfied with the deal to kill the anti-weaponization fund.
item.content:encoded:
Two key Republican rebels are dropping their resistance against President Donald Trump’s pick to lead the Justice Department.

Sens. John Cornyn, R-Texas, and Thom Tillis, R-N.C., have for weeks dug their heels into the ground against confirming acting Attorney General Todd Blanche to fully take over the position. They have been trying to extract concessions from the administration in exchange for their votes.

And those concessions came on Sunday as Blanche’s first key test fast approaches. After warring with Trump and Blanche’s confirmation nearly being withdrawn, the duo are now ready to support the president’s pick to replace former Attorney General Pam Bondi.

TRUMP THREATENS TO YANK HIS OWN AG NOMINEE AS GOP REVOLT GROWS

"We want to express our gratitude to Mr. Blanche and his staff for working with us on this, and we look forward to voting to advance his nomination out of the Senate Judiciary Committee soon," they said in a joint statement.

Cornyn and Tillis had two primary objectives: ensure, in explicit writing, that the nearly $2 billion anti-weaponization fund would not return, and that Trump’s audit immunity would not extend beyond him and the defendants listed in his lawsuit against the IRS.

Blanche announced on Sunday that the anti-weaponization fund was getting the permanent boot, and that the audit protection was going to be narrowly tailored to Trump and his family.

DOJ BARS IRS FROM AUDITING TRUMP’S PRIOR TAX RETURNS IN SETTLEMENT ORDER SIGNED BY BLANCHE

Cornyn and Tillis said they "are pleased" with the Department of Justice’s (DOJ) formal order to deal with both issues, and noted that doing so addressed "concerns that multiple of our Republican colleagues share."

Both issues came from the settlement deal Trump and his family reached with the IRS earlier this year that Blanche helped to roll out.

And both lawmakers are needed to advance Blanche out of committee and onto the Senate floor, given that if either one of them balked against the nominee, he would fail and be stuck in limbo.

TRUMP UNLOADS ON CORNYN, TIES AG NOMINATION FIGHT TO BITTER TEXAS PRIMARY

Cornyn and Tillis both sparred with Trump over the last few days leading up to this moment.

Trump declared that he would withdraw Blanche’s nomination if neither of them broke their resistance. He reupped the pressure over the weekend when he announced that if Blanche’s confirmation continues to stumble or fail, he would revive the anti-weaponization fund and pressure Congress to codify it.

He declared on Truth Social, "I will keep Todd as Acting AG, and push hard to get the Anti-Weaponization Bill," passed through Congress.

Tillis countered that Trump "clearly intends to resurrect the payout pot for punks either by inappropriately establishing another bogus fund or pushing Congress to vote for a bill that the majority of Republicans in the Senate would be against."

"It’s unfortunate that Todd Blanche, who I consider qualified for the job, will not be confirmed because of this reversal," Tillis said over the weekend. "Hopefully, we can resolve this by Tuesday."

With the issues appearing to be resolved, the committee vote on Blanche is moving full steam ahead.

Senate Judiciary Chair Chuck Grassley, R-Iowa, rescheduled the vote for Tuesday after nixing last week’s hearing. A spokesperson for Grassley said his top goal is to see "Todd Blanche’s nomination to be successful."

"Grassley would like to see Blanche confirmed before the August recess as he has an excellent record restoring law and order and keeping Americans safe," they said.

item.title: Nancy Guthrie ransom notes release follows Unabomber ‘precedent' that cracked case, expert says
item.description: A retired investigator says the release of ransom notes in the Nancy Guthrie kidnapping mirrors the 1995 strategy that helped identify the Unabomber.
item.content:encoded:
A veteran retired investigator following the Nancy Guthrie case said the release of two purported ransom notes echoes the investigative strategy that helped identify the Unabomber, as authorities hope the messages will generate new tips six months after her suspected kidnapping in Tucson, Arizona.

"Law enforcement rarely makes the deliberate call to release an offender's own words to the public," said Lisa Miller, a retired investigator from the Colorado Attorney General's Office.

While she's not connected to the Guthrie investigation, she's been following it closely for the past six months.

NANCY GUTHRIE RANSOM DEMANDS RELEASED BY PIMA COUNTY SHERIFF'S DEPARTMENT IN BID TO IDENTIFY SENDER

"The last major precedent: 1995, the Unabomber manifesto…published on the FBI’s recommendation, betting someone would recognize the writing," she noted in an X post over the weekend. "It worked."

GOT A TIP?

David Kaczynski and his wife, Linda Patrik, recognized Ted Kaczynski's writing style and alerted authorities. Ted Kaczynski was arrested in 1996 and pleaded guilty two years later to avoid the death penalty. He spent most of his time behind bars at the ADX Florence Supermax prison in Colorado.

According to FBI records, Kaczynski sent a 35,000-word manifesto outlining his motives "and views of the ills of modern society."

NANCY GUTHRIE CASE COULD HINGE ON MYSTERY TIPSTER WHO EMAILED TMZ

Then-FBI Director Louis Freeh and then-U.S. Attorney General Janet Reno signed off on a plan to publish the document. After it ran in national news, the task force investigating that case received thousands of tips — including a note from David Kaczynski, who included other writing samples that linguistic analysts used to compare against the manifesto.

NANCY GUTHRIE SHERIFF SAYS INVESTIGATORS MAY HAVE MORE VIDEO EVIDENCE AS THEY REVIEW THOUSANDS OF CLIPS

On Friday, the Pima County Sheriff's Department released two notes that have been deemed potentially credible in the abduction of the 84-year-old mother of "Today" co-host Savannah Guthrie.

Authorities said the two notes share a "unique linguistic style" and are believed to have been sent by the same person.

FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X

"There are a number of pieces of information in these notes that just might jar someone to say, 'You know, I've heard that,' or the wording, the style of the writing," Pima County Sheriff Chris Nanos said in a video posted to X Saturday. "We hope that by releasing the actual note, we'll get some response from the community."

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS

They are much shorter than the Unabomber's lengthy essay and less useful for linguistics analysis, Miller said, but they still contain clues and consistent phrasing that could stand out to someone who knows the writer.

The clearest habit appears to be the sender's tendency to write a statement and then immediately follow it with a comma-spliced reinforcing statement, she said.

For example, she gave the following lines:

LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

"You will not be able to contact me from here on out, there will be no negotiation."

"We never intended to hurt her, that was not our intention."

Miller said she doesn't believe the notes were written by artificial intelligence. The notes include "uneven grammar and syntax," emotionally charged repetitions and awkward phrasing, she said.

Authorities are looking for help identifying the masked intruder who appeared on Guthrie's Nest doorbell camera on the night of her abduction as well as the sender of the notes.

Anyone with information in the case is asked to dial 1-800-CALL-FBI or, to remain anonymous, call 520-88-CRIME.

The sum of all rewards in the case is over $1.2 million. The money remained unclaimed as of Friday, a day before the six-month mark since Guthrie's kidnapping.

item.title: Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase defends trans athletes in women's sports as culture war engulfs WNBA
item.description: Four WNBA coaches addressed trans athletes in women's sports within days as protests grow outside games supporting Sophie Cunningham's stance.
item.content:encoded:
A fourth WNBA head coach has addressed the topic of trans athletes in women's sports in a three-day span.

Golden State Valkyries head coach Natalie Nakase became the latest coach to face a question about the issue during a pre-game press conference on Sunday, ahead of the team's win against the Toronto Tempo.

Nakase, who is the reigning WNBA Coach of The Year, was asked about the recent rallies in support of Sophie Cunningham's stance in protecting women's sports. She responded by appearing to defend the inclusion of trans athletes in women's sports.

SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM DOUBLES DOWN AHEAD OF SUN GAME AFTER ESPN PROFILE STIRS CONTROVERSY: 'I SAID WHAT I SAID'

"I think just in terms of how I'm seeing it is, if I can answer, for me sports is about belonging. It’s about inclusivity. It’s about allowing everyone to be their authentic self," Nakase said.

The coach then referenced her ethnicity. Nakase is a third-generation Japanese-American, she previously became the first Asian American to play in the National Women's Basketball League (NWBL).

"I’m big on that because I have been criticized for my height, for my ethnicity. I’ve been in those ‘you shouldn’t belong here,’ [moments] and for me I don’t want that space, especially Golden State, to ever feel like that. "I’m all about women, little girls deserving to play, and that includes trans women. So I’m all about inclusivity."

CHERYL REEVE SENDS CLEAR MESSAGE TO SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM WITH ‘TRANS KIDS BELONG’ SHIRT DURING FEVER-LYNX GAME

Tennis legend Martina Navratilova posted on X that the "ignorance is astounding."

Nakase now joins Indiana Fever coach Stephanie White, Minnesota Lynx Coach Cheryl Reeve and Portland Fire coach Alex Sarama in addressing the issue in recent days.

White, who oversees superstars Caitlin Clark and Sophie Cunningham, gave her answer during a pre-game press conference on Friday.

"I don't know that I would say I'm educated enough from a scientific standpoint. I don't ever believe that exclusion is the answer. I just don't. I do think that when we think about various levels of sport, various governing bodies of sport, and things that go into that, like I said, I'm not educated enough at the different levels. I know growing up I played with the boys all the time," White answered.

Sarama was also asked whether biological males should be allowed to compete in women's sports before his team took on the Fever on Friday, but didn't give a straight answer.

"My focus is as a basketball coach. To be completely honest, I don't think I've ever had to think about that. I'm completely supportive of people from all communities, people from all walks of life, so that's my stance, completely, I'm support of everyone in the Portland community," Sarama said.

Then on Saturday, Reeve was asked ahead of her team's Sunday game against the Fever.

Reeve defended the right of "Save Women’s Sports" demonstrators to gather outside Sunday’s game, but also said that the scenario of "biological men" in girls' locker rooms is "not the case."

"It is not the case that we have 'biological men' in girls' locker rooms. The way it's being phrased, the innuendo there that transgender women are predators of some kind in the locker room. There's a lot of narrative that is problematic that we need to address," she said.

Reeve suggested she is not concerned about any safety issues as a result of the rally.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

"I don’t think we should feel like our safe space is being threatened," Reeve told reporters on Saturday. "I don’t think these demonstrators are not being peaceful, not that I’ve seen. I haven’t seen all of it. I haven’t heard everything that’s happening. But everyone has a right to peacefully assemble, whether you agree with them or not."

The national debate over trans athletes in women's sports has gripped the WNBA after Cunningham revealed her stance on the issue in an ESPN article last month. The three allies that have taken place at Fever games since then have garnered mainstream national attention.

The third rally in Minneapolis on Sunday was the biggest one yet, and featured more confrontational exchanges between the "Save Women's Sports" protesters and the pro-trans counterprotesters than the first two rallies, as seen in footage posted to social media.

item.title: FIFA denies Infantino is seeking Trump administration help as pressure mounts over his leadership
item.description: FIFA denies Gianni Infantino scheduled a call with Marco Rubio as pressure mounts over the collapsed Thrive Capital deal and UEFA's open revolt.
item.content:encoded:
FIFA is pushing back on a New York Post report claiming President Gianni Infantino is turning to the Trump administration for help as he fights to save his job.

A FIFA source told OutKick there is no call scheduled between Infantino and Secretary of State Marco Rubio — or any other member of President Donald Trump’s Cabinet — either Monday or at any other time.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

The source said the Post’s report that such a conversation had been arranged was erroneous.

The New York Post reported Monday that Infantino was scheduled to speak privately with Rubio amid growing pressure over his failed attempt to sell a portion of FIFA’s commercial business to private investors.

According to the Post, the stated purpose of the conversation was to discuss how soccer could serve as a form of American "soft power." However, one source characterized it as an effort by Infantino to secure support for his position.

"He wanted to get online with the secretary and talk about how soccer can be a form of soft power for America," the source told the Post. "But we all know that it is about job protection. It is not about anything else at this point."

The report also claimed Infantino had repeatedly attempted to reach Trump since the controversial proposal collapsed Friday and was seeking prominent "allies" willing to publicly defend him.

FIFA’s source specifically denied that a call with Rubio or another Trump Cabinet official was scheduled. FIFA did not provide an on-the-record statement addressing the Post’s separate claim that Infantino had attempted to contact Trump.

Infantino and Trump have developed a friendship, particularly during this summer’s World Cup in the United States. But Infantino’s current problems center on a proposed company called FIFA Forward Enterprise.

EUROPEAN SOCCER'S GOVERNING BODY FLIPS SPORT UPSIDE DOWN WITH BOYCOTT OF FIFA, FUTURE WORLD CUPS

The new operation would have taken control of FIFA’s broadcasting, sponsorship, licensing and ticketing business.

Thrive Capital, the private equity firm founded by Josh Kushner — the younger brother of Trump son-in-law Jared Kushner — would have purchased a 20% stake for a little more than $4 billion.

Put simply, Infantino wanted to sell private investors a portion of the business responsible for generating much of FIFA’s money.

The proposal reportedly caught several top FIFA officials and national soccer federations by surprise, with many claiming they first learned about it through media reports.

FIFA Chief Operating Officer Kevin Lamour said he felt "deceived" and described the proposal as the work of one man.

The backlash was swift.

UEFA’s 55 European member associations agreed to boycott FIFA competitions while the proposal remained active. The Asian Football Confederation and Concacaf also opposed the plan. UEFA has threatened legal action and instructed FIFA officials to preserve documents and electronic communications connected to it.

Infantino eventually abandoned the proposal Friday, but that has not stopped the revolt against his leadership.

Wales became the first national federation to officially withdraw its support for Infantino’s re-election, citing failures involving governance, leadership, communication and judgment. England has also reportedly withdrawn its backing, while UEFA said Infantino has lost the confidence of world soccer and that "no option should be off the table."

Infantino appeared nearly certain to win another term only weeks ago after reportedly securing pledges from roughly 200 of FIFA’s 211 member federations. He still has significant support in Africa and parts of Asia.

But as opposition continues to build, FIFA says no rescue call with Rubio or another Trump Cabinet official is on the calendar.

item.title: Mamdani’s city grocery plan could leave taxpayers paying for every banana
item.description: Zohran Mamdani's government grocery stores promise 30% discounts, but critics warn taxpayers will cover massive losses in a razor-thin margin industry.
item.content:encoded:
Thirty-five years after the Soviet Union collapsed, the Communist bread line is poised for a comeback in the Big Apple, as Mayor Zohran Mamdani announces his government grocery stores will be undercutting real groceries by 30%. Not to worry, socialism will work this time.

The announcement came during a press conference on July 27, where Comrade Mamdani promised 30% discounts for "essential" products at his new city-run grocery stores. The problem, of course, is grocery stores are in a razor-thin industry, sporting profit margins of roughly 2%. And that's with competent management, which New York City government is decidedly not famous for.

That means even if the socialists somehow manage to run a grocery as efficiently as Aldi, Walmart or Gristedes, the city will be losing an ungodly amount of money — at least 28 cents on the dollar. Since New York’s best and brightest in government will be far less efficient than the private sector, the losses, predictably, will be even higher.

EXPERTS SCORCH MAMDANI'S GROCERY PLAN AS AN 'ILLUSION' THAT WILL HAVE TAXPAYERS FOOTING THE BILL

Of course, operating in the red for a government establishment means taxpayers get stuck with the tab. The losses of Comrade Mamdani’s state-run enterprises will be covered by New Yorkers’ tax dollars — derived from tax rates that are already among the nation’s highest.

And that's where the fun begins. If city groceries were genuinely selling food 30% cheaper, that would rob enough market share from real grocery stores that they would start going out of business. After all, private stores must pay rent, property taxes, insurance, labor, utilities, security and New York’s regulatory army.

Conversely, Mamdani’s stores get city property tax exemptions, and apparently an unlimited allowance from dad who's willing to lose 28 cents on the dollar. Marginal supermarkets will close while others will cancel plans to open.

And what stops anyone from buying deeply discounted groceries for resale? After all, 30% off is cheaper than wholesale. Will Mamdani then prohibit purchases by grocers? Good luck telling who’s who in the checkout line since asking for ID is racist in New York.

NY GOVERNOR HOPEFUL VOWS SHOWDOWN WITH MAMDANI OVER SOCIALIST AGENDA: ‘I WILL STOP HIM’

Then we enter Act Three: What happens when taxpayers get tired of the money pit? Every time New York has seized an industry, it turned into a money loser. New York's city-run transit system — MTA — replaced private-sector alternatives that used to be profitable with a government-run system that loses $11.7 billion a year — roughly $3,000 per household in New York City. That’s how much the government has to subsidize the MTA to keep it running.

If city groceries approach that number, there will inevitably be calls for subsidy cuts. Given the mandate to keep groceries cheap combined with the costs of government efficiency, that means the groceries will have to cut back on quality. No longer a giant money pit, they’ll become slightly smaller money pits full of rotting food.

When the smoke clears, New Yorkers get a couple years of cheap bananas, tens of millions of dollars in new debt and real companies fleeing, so residents have to take two trains and a bus to get to a real grocery store.

In fact, this is exactly what's happened in dozens of government grocery experiments across the country, from Kansas City — which lost $18 million on a grocery that sold rotting food — to Chicago — which blew $26 million running seven stores into the ground. But socialism will work this time if Comrade Mamdani smiles hard enough.

Instead of recreating Soviet breadlines on the taxpayer dime, Mamdani should sit down with functioning grocery stores and ask how he can help them expand. For example, reducing property taxes, permitting costs and construction costs.

He could relax parking rules and stop converting every curb into a dedicated bus lane. Disused public space could be leased at a discount to real grocery stores. Enact zoning reform so groceries don't wait years in limbo for the ministry of red tape to green-light a location. Perhaps Mamdani could even try arresting shoplifters occasionally.

The hallmark of socialism is it breaks things, then uses the detritus as an excuse to break more things. New York already has a distinct absence of proper grocery stores thanks to dysfunctional local government. Handing that bureaucracy the entire food supply will turn an annoyance into a crisis.

item.title: Charlotte repeat offender charged with killing man hours after release on bond
item.description: David Simpson allegedly shot two men in Charlotte less than two hours after his bond release from Mecklenburg County Jail on an unrelated charge.
item.content:encoded:
A convicted killer allegedly shot two men, killing one, less than two hours after he was released from a North Carolina jail on bond last week, a stunning timeline that is raising fresh questions about why the repeat violent offender was free in the first place.

David Simpson, 29, is charged with first-degree murder, attempted first-degree murder, assault with a deadly weapon with intent to kill inflicting serious injury, and possession of a firearm by a felon in the July 29 shooting at an east Charlotte apartment complex. A Mecklenburg County judge on Friday ordered that he be held without bond.

Court records obtained by WCNC show Simpson was released from the Mecklenburg County Jail at 12:20 a.m. after posting a $10,000 bond on an unrelated charge of possession of a weapon by a prisoner. Police said the shooting happened less than two hours later, around 1:45 a.m., leaving one man dead and another seriously wounded.

HOUSE DEMOCRAT BLASTED AFTER EARLY RELEASE LAW FREED INMATES LATER CHARGED WITH MURDER

Police said the shooting followed a long-running dispute over a parking space outside the apartment complex. Officers had already been called to the property twice that night after arguments broke out between the victims and residents over where they had parked.

Surveillance video cited in the documents appears to show Simpson outside with his girlfriend when the victims' SUV drove past. Detectives said Simpson went inside, returned carrying what they described as a weighted black bag, and ran toward the victims.

About 10 minutes later, two gunshots can be heard on the video. Roughly 30 seconds after that, Simpson is seen jogging back toward his apartment while handling the bag before driving away, investigators said. Officers recovered two spent 7.62-caliber rifle casings at the scene.

CRAZY BRAWL OVER A PARKING SPOT IN NEW YORK INCLUDES A VICIOUS SKATEBOARD TO THE HEAD

One victim died at the scene. The second made it inside an apartment before collapsing and later underwent surgery.

Court records show Simpson was previously charged with first-degree murder in a 2013 fatal shooting but pleaded guilty to voluntary manslaughter in 2015, Queen City News reported. He served about five years in prison before being released on parole in 2020.

Since then, he has been arrested several more times, including on multiple charges of possession of a firearm by a felon, WBTV reported.

DEMOCRATIC BOSTON COUNCILOR RIPS 'SOFT-ON-CRIME' POLICIES AFTER SUSPECTED GUNMAN'S VIOLENT PAST REVEALED

He also had pending charges this year for possession of a firearm by a felon, resisting a public officer and misdemeanor larceny, WCNC reported, citing court records.

Charlotte defense attorney Tim Cannady, who is not involved in the case, questioned why Simpson remained free despite his history.

"If you look at his history, it seems like this gentleman has picked up just about every year up to this point some kind of a violent crime," Cannady told WCNC. "So you kind of have to ask the question: Why wasn't he already in jail?"

Former Charlotte City Council member Tariq Bokhari offered a similar criticism.

"We know what these top 1% of repeat offenders are going to do, and for some reason, we just don't have the appetite to take action," Bokhari told WBTV. "It feels like 'Groundhog Day,' to be quite honest."

Simpson refused to leave his jail cell for his first scheduled court appearance Friday morning, delaying the hearing until a judge ordered him to appear later that afternoon.

His girlfriend, Shakema Scott, has also been charged with accessory after the fact.

Simpson is due back in court on Aug. 21.

item.title: NASCAR fans rip social media post for obvious reason, Jeff Gordon's biggest regret & race wife hits the beach
item.description: NASCAR's viral social media post featuring Cole Custer and John Hunter Nemechek drew nearly 6 million views but exposed a glaring double standard.
item.content:encoded:
Monday Morning Pit-Stop is a weekly NASCAR column that runs on OutKick.com and Fox News Digital. If you're looking for a normal NASCAR recap, go check out insufferable ESPN ... assuming they still know NASCAR exists.

First Monday of August and we don't even have a NASCAR race to complain about today. What are we supposed to do now?

Feels weird, doesn't it? The NASCAR Cup Series season is the longest in all of sports, with — by far — the fewest down time. The fellas get two(ish) off weeks a season, give or take, and that's about it from February through October.

So when the series is off, it's a bit of a shock to the system. It just doesn't happen. Hand up, I actually forgot it was an off week yesterday afternoon and started reflexively looking for the race at around 3 p.m.

I couldn't take anymore of the trans talk from the WNBA, and I needed something to put on while I yanked weeds from the back deck.

NASCAR SENDS LOUD MESSAGE TO AMERICA-HATING LOSERS, BLACK DRIVER'S CONTROVERSIAL PAINT SCHEME & DRUNK JIMMIE!

Crickets. Nothing. Dead air.

You never know what you have have till it's gone.

Anyway, this award-winning (allegedly) column doesn't take weeks off, so we're here, ready to turn the page toward the rest of the season. Daytona is just a few weeks away, you know.

How should we fill the space? How about this social media post from NASCAR that absolutely blew up the internet over the weekend? Fans were quick to call them out, and I don't blame them.

What else? I've got Jeff Gordon giving us a rare insight into his relationship with the late, great Dale Earnhardt, Samantha Busch reminiscing on some early days with Kyle, and McCall Gaulding spending the off week in Costa Rica.

Sound good? Good!

Four tires, enough fuel to get us to Iowa, and maybe a few more off weeks for the fellas throughout the year, because two(ish) ain't enough ... Monday Morning Pit-Stop — the 'NASCAR Finally Goes Viral, But The Double Standard Is Glaring' edition — is LIVE!

There it is! That's the post that set the internet ablaze this weekend.

Good for NASCAR for being part of the news cycle on an off weekend, though. Credit where it's due. Bad PR is still PR.

Just ask the WNBA.

That above moment is from a decade ago (time flies!), when Cole Custer sprinted across the track and attacked John Hunter Nemechek after the two wrecked each other at the finish. I can't believe it's been 10 years since that moment.

I'm tell you, folks, you blink and a decade has passed. Lordy.

Anyway, it was an iconic moment in NASCAR history (not really), and, for some reason, the interns who run the main account posted it Friday. Naturally, it went mega-viral to the tune of nearly 6 million views, with big-time personalities such as Pat McAfee even reposting it:

Again, PR is PR, and when you get Pat McAfee to repost a 10-year-old truck race on a random Saturday in August, you're doing something right.

That being said, hardcore fans were QUICK to point out the double standard by NASCAR — and it's one that I've pointed out for years.

NASCAR routinely promotes this stuff on its social media accounts. Remember the infamous Kyle Busch-Ricky Stenhouse Jr. fight a few years back? The social media team(s) gobbled that up ... for days! They milked it for all it was worth.

At the same time, though, the sanctioning body will also A) fine drivers for this behavior, B) dock them points, C) sometimes suspend them, and D) discourage it entirely on the track.

You can't have your cake and eat it, too!

I could go on and on. Seriously, NASCAR fans are nothing if not consistent in their bitching and moaning.

Look, I get it. It seems odd to promote this stuff off the track, but actively discourage it on the track and after races. That being said, the social media team and the actual folks who run the sport are in two very separate buildings. Hell, I'm on even sure they're on the same property!

Two different bottom lines, and two very different goals. I see it here at OutKick all the time. The social team's job is to create content, and clicks, and engagement. They don't care about the Xs and Os of stuff and how the sausage is made. They care about the impressions.

That being said, I also think NASCAR should just let this stuff happen and leave it alone. Let the boys police themselves — on and off the track.

When was the last time a NASCAR social media post got 6 million pageviews? Probably something to consider.

OK, let's move this class along ...

Speaking of the good old days of NASCAR — when men were MEN! — let's check in with Jeff Gordon and ... Dale Earnhardt?

"If I had time with him again before we lost him, what would I have said to him? What would I have asked him?" Gordon said last week on the 'Bussin With The Boys' podcast.

"I definitely would've said, 'Hey, '95 when we were going for the championship, how much of that was just total bulls–t? It was getting under my skin. I would do an interview, and they go, 'We were just talking to Dale, and Dale said Rainbow Warrior, Wonder Boy, and all these nicknames he had for me.

"'He can't win the championship, what are they going to do, serve milk at the championship? I didn't want to get involved in that. And I kinda wish I had a little bit more, because I do think he was doing it because he knew it was working.

"Not just to get under my skin, but it was working for the media, it was working for NASCAR, and the growth and the fans.

"I think that's what I'd love to know is, how much of that was manufactured?"

Dale, by the way, would've probably loved NASCAR's post from over the weekend. Like Jeff said, Dale knew what he was doing. He knew what worked, and what played on TV, and what lit fires. He knew how to get eyeballs to the screen, and, more importantly, how to keep 'em there.

The Dale Earnhardt-Jeff Gordon rivalry from the late 1990s was peak NASCAR, in my opinion. That's when the sport was exploding. When it was bigger than the NFL, if you believe that.

And yes, Jeff should've engaged a little more. Duh. Always engage, folks.

Hope every driver in the garage reads that today.

OK, two more quickies on the way out. First? Samantha Busch has been slowly returning to social media since Kyle's death two months ago (goodness), and it's a gut-punch of a post every single time.

After last week's race at Indy, Samantha revealed that's where her and Kyle first met nearly 20 years ago:

"These photos were taken later that year in 2007, and looking at them now, I see two kids completely caught up in the excitement of falling in love, with absolutely no idea what was ahead of us," she wrote. "We grew up together. We built a life together. Through every season, every challenge, and every dream, we just kept choosing each other.

"I look at these pictures and wish I could tell that 21-year-old girl to soak up every single second. She never could have imagined how beautiful our life would become, or that one day she’d be wishing for just one more day with you."

Goodness gracious. Like I said, just a punch straight to the gut. I can't believe it's been two months. Wonder what Kyle would've thought of NASCAR's post over the weekend?

OK, that's it for today. Good work, everyone. We made it through the final NASCAR off week of 2026.

Zane Smith's wife, McCall Gaulding, checks in from Costa Rica, and takes us home.

See you at Iowa.

item.title: Idaho In-N-Out Burger shooting motive still a mystery as armed citizen speaks out
item.description: An armed citizen and off-duty trooper returned fire at the Twin Falls In-N-Out Burger gunman, who was reportedly shocked by the armed response.
item.content:encoded:
Police are still working to determine why a 24-year-old gunman opened fire at a crowded In-N-Out Burger in Twin Falls, Idaho, killing three people and wounding seven others before taking his own life after taking fire from a bystander and an off-duty Idaho state trooper.

Twin Falls Police Chief Matthew Hicks said Sunday that investigators were confident Chad Williams acted alone in Saturday's attack, but detectives had not yet established a motive or fully traced his movements before the shooting.

"We believe their actions helped drive the suspect away from the scene, preventing further casualties," Hicks said of an armed citizen and officer who returned fire. "We want to take a moment and commend the actions of the off-duty officer and the citizen, and their heroic action to stop this incident."

Police have not publicly identified the trooper or the bystander, but the Idaho Statesman detailed the heroics of Jordan Salinas, 35, of Kimberly, Idaho, strapped by the shoulder with a FN Five-seveN semi-automatic pistol fitted with a suppressor.

OFF-DUTY TROOPER AND ARMED CITIZEN HAILED AS HEROES AFTER RETURNING FIRE ON IN-N-OUT GUNMAN

Salinas, a reported "healthcare worker, the full-time caregiver of his wheelchair-bound brother," told the paper he took up gun training after a 2021 shooting – never even aiming a gun at an animal – saying he was able to "observe," "orient" and "decide" that "OK, this is the guy," he said before being resolute to "act."

The gunman, he said, was shocked by the armed response.

"He did not like it when bullets started firing both ways," Salinas, whose girlfriend at the restaurant was stuck in Williams fire, told the Statesman, adding he felt "no fear."

"There’s a task that needs to be done, and we’re the ones who need to do it," he added, only standing down when he said police took over the scene, thinking, "OK, my part is done."

The shooter was found dead from a self-inflicted gunshot wound near the restaurant, according to police.

MULTIPLE PEOPLE KILLED IN SHOOTING AT IDAHO IN-N-OUT RESTAURANT, SUSPECT DEAD

"These people are true heroes in our community," Twin Falls County Sheriff Jack Johnson said. "They diverted the shooter and without a doubt saved many lives."

Hicks said Williams' family was cooperating with authorities. Detectives were examining his activities before the shooting and trying to determine whether any victims had been deliberately targeted.

Authorities said seven people were injured. Two remained in critical condition Sunday, three were listed as stable and two had been treated and released from a hospital.

Officials said both fired at Williams during what authorities described as a chaotic and fast-moving attack, diverting his attention from the restaurant as customers and employees fled.

IN-N-OUT PRESIDENT SAYS ‘HEART IS BROKEN’ AFTER EMPLOYEE, CUSTOMERS KILLED IN IDAHO SHOOTING

Witness Lane Koehn, 34, said he was stopped at a traffic light near the restaurant when he saw a man carrying an AR-style rifle emerge from the drive-thru. Another man armed with a handgun then began firing at the shooter, Koehn told The Associated Press.

Koehn said he later saw an In-N-Out employee drag a wounded co-worker across the parking lot. The injured worker had been shot in the chest, he said.

"She was pretty bad off, but I don’t know. I hope she made it," Koehn said.

One of the three people killed was an In-N-Out employee, company owner Lynsi Snyder confirmed in a statement. Officials had not released the victims’ identities as they worked to notify relatives.

"My heart is broken, my chest is heavy, my eyes burn from the tears I’ve shed," Snyder said. "We lost one of our beautiful associates tonight."

"In-N-Out will be mourning with the families and praying for them as they tread through a very painful season."

Snyder said the employee had been caring for customers when she was killed. The company was working with police and offering support to victims, employees and their families.

The shooting erupted Saturday afternoon at the recently opened restaurant in a busy commercial area where hundreds of shoppers, diners and employees were believed to have been present.

Twin Falls resident Haley Dodaro said she and her mother were waiting in the drive-thru when they saw workers running from the restaurant and people fleeing across the road.

"At first," Dodaro said, she thought there might have been a fire. A person directing traffic then warned them that there was an active shooter.

"People were running out crying and screaming," she said. "It was very scary."

Nayeli Rodriguez, who was inside the restaurant with her daughters, said an employee told customers to get down after gunfire was heard near the kitchen. An older man tried to shield Rodriguez and her children before they escaped.

"We were trying to get as far as we could, and some angels let us in their car," Rodriguez said.

A local taxi company said one of its drivers, Terry Dudley, was shot twice in the back while charging his Tesla near the restaurant. North Star Taxi said Dudley survived but faced "a very long road ahead."

Salinas posted a humble Facebook message urging focus on "victims, their families, and everyone affected."

"The last 24 hours have been overwhelming," the message posted late Sunday night read. "I want to sincerely thank my family, friends, and everyone who has reached out with messages, prayers, and support. I haven't been able to respond to everyone yet, but please know I've seen your messages, and they mean more to me than I can put into words.

"In the coming days, I'll share a more complete account of what happened, to the best of my recollection, when I'm able.

"For now, my heart remains with the victims, their families, and everyone affected by yesterday's tragedy. Thank you for continuing to keep them in your thoughts and prayers, and thank you all for the incredible support you've shown me and my family."

The FBI asked members of the public to submit photographs and video recorded during the attack. Twin Falls police also urged anyone who witnessed the shooting or had relevant information to contact investigators.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Jadeveon Clowney's career filled with high expectations is now supposed to deliver a Houston Texans Super Bowl
item.description: Jadeveon Clowney rejoins the Houston Texans talking Super Bowl, but his 12-year career history suggests fans should temper their expectations.
item.content:encoded:
Jadeveon Clowney is back with the Houston Texans, an addition that comes with much attention, and the expectation of fielding the NFL's best defense. and Super Bowl talk.

But, please, pump the brakes.

Because if there's one thing Clowney's 12-year career has taught us, it is that high expectations have too often gone unrealized.

The one-time No. 1 overall selection in the NFL Draft spent this offseason as a valued free agent until he agreed on Sunday to rejoin the Texans, the team that originally drafted him in 2014.

HOUSTON TEXANS' 2025 WIN TOTAL SET AT 9.5 AS CJ STROUD FACES QUESTIONS ABOUT OFFENSIVE LINE

And, true to form, Clowney arrives with commotion and fanfare for great things ahead. Fans are aflutter that this familiar name is aboard for the coming season and Clowney is doing nothing to minimize the excitement by talking about a Super Bowl.

"I can help contribute and (we have) a good chance to chase a Super Bowl," Clowney told KPRC 2 Houston.

In another interview Clowney said he's learned to lead during his career and knows what it takes to get to a Super Bowl.

So, lotta high expectations, y'all.

Except this is where the Clowney reality begs caution. Because Clowney has never won a Super Bowl. He's never played in a Super Bowl.

And while that doesn't prevent him from helping the Texans in 2026, he won't be leading the charge. He'll be supporting starters Will Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter who were both top 10 in sacks last season.

NFL GREAT AARON DONALD MAY COME OUT OF RETIREMENT TO JOIN MYLES GARRETT ON RAMS' DEFENSE, EX-TEAMMATE SAYS

Clowney is a piece to the puzzle on a defense that was No. 2 in fewest points allowed last season behind the Seattle Seahawks. He's not the signature piece.

"We're continuously trying to build depth, especially in that room because of the way we play and stylistically what we ask those guys to do," said Texans defensive coordinator Matt Burke. "It is important. It's important for us to be able to keep guys fresh and to keep Danielle and Will and those guys throwing fastballs through the whole game. The depth piece is an important piece for us."

The Texans and Clowney agreed to a one-year deal worth $5.5 million. The deal includes incentives that could push that money higher.

But this isn't about money for Clowney, who had been negotiating with multiple teams including the Cleveland Browns.

Clowney lives in Houston, so it makes sense for him. And he loves the idea of playing for Texans coach DeMeco Ryans.

"I was looking forward to playing for DeMeco," Clowney said. "Pretty exciting coach to play for. I reached out to him and told him I wanted to play for him,

"It was a family decision. It wasn't about the money, it was about chasing my legacy and chasing a Super Bowl. I've got a lot of game left and I want to contribute."

Clowney returns to Houston, in part, because of its head coach. He was traded by Houston just prior to the 2019 season, in part, because he feuded with coach Bill O'Brien.

Clowney was picked with the No. 1 overall selection in the 2014 NFL Draft to be perhaps an all-timer and definitely a perennial Pro Bowler. But that's not what happened.

He earned three Pro Bowl invites, the last one coming in 2018. He didn't turn into the unstoppable sack-machine the Texans originally hoped, indeed, he's a more consistent run-stopper than pass rusher.

Clowney wasn't even the best pass rusher or defensive lineman in 2014 because Khalil Mack and Aaron Donald were selected later in that fateful draft. Clowney has never delivered a double-digit sack season.

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST SPORTS NEWS

So the player selected to be a franchise cornerstone has bounced around with seven teams.

This all, of course, serves as a sober caution: High expectations and Jadeveon Clowney have been constant companions in the NFL and the current Super Bowl talk in Houston continues that.

But the history is the history.

item.title: Once-hidden coastal town facing disruption as social media influencers transform local life
item.description: Some Nantucket locals are pushing back against influencers and overtourism as the tiny island's streets, parking lots and beaches feel increasingly unrecognizable.
item.content:encoded:
A battle is brewing on a tiny luxury island 30 miles off the coast of Massachusetts, according to many reports. 

Gorgeous scenes of Nantucket have been nearly impossible to miss lately on TikTok and Instagram, with images of weathered-gray cottages, colorful hydrangeas and pristine beaches populating social media platforms. 

Yet the island has seen tourism explode, according to some residents and longtime visitors — and locals say they've become inundated by visitors, crowds and noise.

WEALTHY SUMMER SANCTUARY LIMITS TOURISTS, HIRES PATROL 'DOCENTS' TO KEEP OUTSIDERS IN CHECK

"[Nantucket] has become something it wasn't before," a 23-year-old lifetime Nantucket resident, who asked for anonymity, told Fox News Digital. "It was kind of like a rustic New England vacation spot, and it's been changing for the last 20 years."

The person added, "It's transforming into something that [residents] don't recognize, and it makes them very upset."

With no bridge to the island, visitors cannot drive or take a train. Nantucket is accessible exclusively by air and sea, requiring travelers to arrive by ferry or plane, per the Town of Nantucket.

For decades, that lack of accessibility kept crowds in check. 

DEADLY BACTERIA FOUND IN WATERS NEAR LUXURY VACATION DESTINATION AHEAD OF SUMMER

"You either have to fly or take the ferry," J.Q. Louise, a Boston-based travel influencer who has visited Nantucket several times, told Fox News Digital. 

"I think that's what's kept it exclusive for so many years," she said.

That appears to be changing, as the island typically draws an estimated 2 million visitors annually, according to the Nantucket Current.

Recent complaints about influencers reached a fever pitch when a longtime shop owner hung a sign saying, "No Influencers."

Store owner John Sylvia posted the sign at Four Winds Craft Guild, his Nantucket antiques and artisan shop.

MAJOR CITY LAUNCHES HARSH TOURIST CRACKDOWN AS LOCALS REVOLT OVER MASSIVE CROWDS

"I feel sometimes my store is used as someone’s background, a stage," Sylvia told The New York Times.

"I don't have this hatred toward influencers," he clarified. "It was more of a joke. It is a problem we should look at as a society."

Sylvia's partner, Jessica Jenkins, told the outlet she feels deluged by "people creating videos on corners of themselves sipping an iced coffee and looking over their shoulder and doing a shoe kick or whatever."

Fox News Digital reached out to Four Winds Craft Guild for further comment.

FAMOUS BEACH NOW REQUIRES VISITORS TO RESERVE SPOTS WEEKS AHEAD AND PAY FEES

Content creators such as Paige Lorenze are defending themselves.

"If you call yourself a feminist but proudly put up a 'No Influencers' sign, it’s worth asking who you are attempting to delegitimize, and why," Lorenze, who owns a boutique near Four Winds Craft Guild, commented on a now-deleted Instagram post.

"I have no issue with [John Sylvia's] shop, and I hope people keep walking in and supporting island craftspeople," Lorenze told The Cut. 

"I just think Nantucket’s story is more generous than that sign." 

Fox News Digital reached out to Paige Lorenze for further comment.

In the spring, the Siasconset Civic Association, a nonprofit community advocacy organization, proposed recommendations to curb overcrowding. The Nantucket Select Board designated specific visiting hours on the footpath for July and August.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

"Bluff docents" — called rangers in an earlier version of the proposal — were approved to keep an eye on activity, according to Nantucket Current. 

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

The Sconset Civic Association also proposed turnstiles or gates at entrances, but those weren't approved.

A Reddit post on the Nantucket debate generated hundreds of comments.

"My family has a house there, and trust me when I say the entire island has no need for influencers or to go viral," a Reddit user said.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The "island gets so crowded during the summer that even cottage industries have popped up to handle the crowds," the commenter added.

A Connecticut resident who has spent summers in Sconset for 38 years also said the island feels different.

"The crowds are flashy, but they have more to spend," the person, who asked to remain anonymous, told Fox News Digital.

J.Q. Louise believes the tiny size of the island — it's about 14 miles long and 3.5 miles wide — magnifies the problem.

"It kind of felt like a hidden gem, and it definitely isn't hidden anymore," she said.

Fox News Digital reached out to the town of Nantucket, Siasconset Civic Association and Nantucket Island Chamber of Commerce for comment. 

Ashley J. DiMella and Jessica Mekles of Fox News Digital contributed reporting.
